chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Poverty does not enter a house in which the names of Muhammad, Ahmad, Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, or Ja'far, or Talib, or Abd Allah, or Fatimah (from among the women), peace be upon them, are present.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu al-Hasan (Title of Imam Musa al-Kadhim or Imam Ali al-Rida depending on context, here referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of bearing the names of the Ahl al-Bayt in a household according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) links the presence of the Ahl al-Bayt's names in a home to divine protection from poverty, reflecting the Shia belief in the barakah (blessing) inherent in the Prophet's lineage. This concept is often understood not merely as material wealth but as spiritual sufficiency and resilience against hardship, reinforcing the status of the Imams as sources of grace for their followers.
